sources.title: Global smooth solution curves using rigorous branch following
sources.read_scope: Introduction and section 2, printed pp. 5-10: equations (13)-(20), Definition 6, Lemmas 5 and 7, Proposition 8 and connecting proof; section 1.2/3 opening for fold qualification.
primary_findings: A bijective approximate inverse and uniform residual/derivative bounds give a unique smooth parameterized zero in a predictor tube.
Strict radii inequalities hold across the parameter interval, not only at sampled parameter values.
Adjacent certified pieces require a verified same-root connection; Proposition 8 supplies nested enclosures.
sources.application_scope: General C1 framework can be specialized to a finite-dimensional source residual. Explicit model envelopes remain the authors' work.
sources.source_notation_note: Both retrieved PDF text representations render the shifted-map line in Lemma 7 without the predictor subtraction needed for its stated origin-centered codomain. This is an observed extracted-text omission; a typesetting versus extraction cause was not separately established. The preceding fixed-point and tube definitions identify the required coordinate translation. The screenshot tool returned only an image marker, so no visual confirmation is claimed.
sources.not_read: No full-paper reading or reproduction of numerical examples is claimed.

sources.title: Validated continuation for equilibria of PDEs
sources.read_source: Author-hosted 27-page manuscript; header retains 200X typesetting placeholders
sources.read_scope: Printed pp. 3-6, section 2, equations (2.1)-(2.6), Theorem 2.1 and proof; introduction distinguishes floating-point timing studies and interval-validated results.
primary_findings: A normalized weighted sup norm turns an unequal-width box into a unit ball.
Component bounds on the center defect and a full-box Lipschitz map establish self-mapping and contraction.
Uniform supremum below one is required in the sequence-space theorem; finitely many strict component inequalities give the corresponding finite-dimensional condition.
sources.application_scope: Finite component/block weights are a standard specialization. Fixed weights and actual global derivative bounds are required.
sources.version_note: The older Rutgers 2005 URL is a second version of the same work, not an additional paper. Only the McGill manuscript's numbered theorem is used.
sources.not_read: No claim to execute or audit its PDE numerical examples.

sources.title: Verified solution of large systems and global optimization problems
sources.publication: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 60 (1-2), 201-218, 20 June 1995
sources.read_scope: Printed pp. 2-6, interval isotonicity/rounding and section 3 equations (3.1)-(3.9), Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and following parameter discussion.
primary_findings: Approximate inverse, residual inclusion and interval derivative/slope enclosure lead to strict Krawczyk inclusion and existence/regularity.
Theorem 3.2 uses the special centered enclosure (3.6) and explicitly states existence/regularity; do not silently append full-box uniqueness to this version.
Floating-point and transcendental enclosures require proper rounding; interval dependency can overestimate the true range.
sources.application_scope: The proposed full-box Jacobian contraction supplies an explicit uniqueness route. A converged approximate corrector alone is not an inclusion proof.
sources.metadata_note: Venue/year/pages confirmed from publisher and institutional results in EXA06-Q4, not inferred from Ru95b filename. Exa's secondary catalog date differs; primary date is used.
